probmed

PR validation uses the full local gate, which posts a commit-specific required status after passing. GitHub Actions still publishes the website on main; R-CMD-check remains required on main PRs until branch protection is switched, while coverage is manual.

probmed provides a robust framework for computing PmedP_{med}, a scale-free probabilistic effect size for causal mediation analysis.

What is PmedP_{med}?

PmedP_{med} offers an intuitive alternative to traditional mediation effect sizes. With treatment held at its treated level xx for both potential outcomes, it is the probability that the outcome when the mediator takes its treated level M(x)M(x) exceeds the outcome when it takes its control level M(x*)M(x^*), with ties counted as one half: P(Y(x,M(x))>Y(x,M(x*)))+12P(Y(x,M(x))=Y(x,M(x*)))P(Y(x, M(x)) > Y(x, M(x^*))) + \tfrac12 P(Y(x, M(x)) = Y(x, M(x^*))). The direct effect cancels, so PmedP_{med} is mediation-only.

Unlike the “Proportion Mediated” or simple indirect effect coefficients, PmedP_{med}: * Is Scale-Free: Interpretable regardless of the units of measurement for XX, MM, or YY. * Is Bounded: Always falls between 0 and 1, with 0.5 meaning no mediation effect, making it comparable across studies. * Handles Non-Linearity: Can be extended to Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) where coefficients are not directly comparable.

Features

Single-mediator plug-in calls honor an explicit seed. MBCO is deterministic and reports numerical statuses in result@diagnostics; only verified likelihood-ratio endpoints set converged = TRUE, and detected disconnected sets or failed profiles return missing interval bounds. Parallel mediation keeps its legacy inversion path.

  • Flexible Modeling: Gaussian (identity link) and binary (logit or probit link) mediators and outcomes, with covariates. Binary models are standardized over the observed covariate rows. Other families (Poisson, ordinal, …), interactions and transformed treatment/mediator terms are rejected with an informative error rather than simulated incorrectly.
  • Comprehensive Effect Reporting: Provides both PmedP_{med} (probabilistic effect size) and the traditional Indirect Effect (a×ba \times b) with bootstrap confidence intervals.
  • Robust Inference: Implements multiple methods for constructing confidence intervals:
    • Parametric Bootstrap: Efficient and accurate for large samples with known distributions.
    • Nonparametric Bootstrap: Robust to distributional assumptions (resampling-based).
    • Plug-in Estimator: Fast point estimation.
    • MBCO (Gaussian): deterministic likelihood-ratio interval with verified endpoints. It never undercovers but is conservative near the double null, flagged by @diagnostics$pmed$near_double_null.
    • Model-based bootstrap (opt-in, method = "model_bootstrap"): refits both equations on data simulated from the fitted models, so residual scales are re-estimated too. Coverage varies by design; see docs/reports/CALIBRATION-2026-10-14.md in the repository.
  • Modern Architecture: Built on the S7 object-oriented system, ensuring type safety, stability, and easy extensibility.
  • Ecosystem Integration: Works seamlessly with popular R packages:
    • lavaan: Extract from Structural Equation Models with FIML and robust estimators
    • mediation: Direct integration with mediate() objects
    • Standard lm/glm: Native support for regression models
  • User-Friendly Interface: Designed to work with standard R formula interfaces and data.frame inputs.

Modern estimands

Beyond the core pmed(), the package ships cross-fitted, influence-function-based estimators, each with its own S7 result class. See the Modern estimands article for details and caveats.

Function Result class What it estimates
ward_residual() GaugePmedResult Gauge-calibrated P_med (residual over observed effect) with weak-identification gates
incr_pmed(), incr_sensitivity() IncrPmedResult Incremental P_med and its per-delta tipping analysis
sobol_pmed() SobolPmedResult Sobol variance-scale P_med
wasserstein_pmed() WassersteinPmedResult Wasserstein proportion mediated
rg_flow_contrast() RgFlowResult Scale-indexed NIE/TE with cluster-robust inference
pmed_sensitivity() PmedSensitivity Unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding (tipping point)

Status and known limitations

Version 0.4.0 (GitHub release only; not submitted to CRAN). For the binary Wasserstein proportion mediated, estimation near an exactly zero mediation path is hard: the plug-in bias is of order n−1/4n^{-1/4}, none of the point estimators tested met the frozen bias gate (|bias|/SD < .10) there, and that gate was shown to be infeasible for any estimator with values in [0, 1] in the zero-direct and weak-direct cells at n = 500, and the Fieller interval is the supported uncertainty statement. See the boundary article section and docs/reports/REPORT-boundary-point-risk-2026-10-21.md.

Installation

Install from the Data-Wise r-universe — no compiler needed, and dependencies (e.g. medfit) resolve automatically:

install.packages("probmed", repos = "https://data-wise.r-universe.dev")

Or install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("data-wise/probmed")

Quick Example

Here is a basic example showing how to simulate data and compute PmedP_{med} using a parametric bootstrap approach.

1. Simulate Data

First, we generate a dataset with a continuous treatment (XX), mediator (MM), and outcome (YY), along with a covariate (CC).

library(probmed)

set.seed(123)
n <- 300
data <- data.frame(X = rnorm(n), C = rnorm(n))

# Mediator model: M ~ X + C
data$M <- 0.5 * data$X + 0.3 * data$C + rnorm(n)

# Outcome model: Y ~ M + X + C
data$Y <- 0.4 * data$M + 0.2 * data$X + 0.2 * data$C + rnorm(n)

2. Compute PmedP_{med}

We use the pmed() function to estimate the effect size. We specify the models for the outcome and mediator, and select the bootstrap method.

result <- pmed(
  Y ~ X + M + C,             # Outcome model formula
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,     # Mediator model formula
  data = data,
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap",
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = 42
)

3. View Results

The results object provides a clear summary of both PmedP_{med} and the Indirect Effect with confidence intervals.

print(result)
#>
#> P_med: Probability of Mediated Shift
#> ====================================
#>
#> Estimate: 0.55
#> 95% CI: [0.53, 0.572]
#>
#> Indirect Effect (Product of Coefficients):
#> Estimate: 0.2
#> 95% CI: [0.129, 0.283]
#>
#> Inference: parametric_bootstrap
#> Bootstrap samples: 1000
#>
#> Treatment contrast: X = 1 vs. X* = 0
#>
#> Interpretation:
#>   P(Y(1, M(1)) > Y(1, M(0))) = 0.55
#>   P that the mediator shift (M(0) -> M(1)) leaves a random individual better off, holding X = 1.

summary(result)

Interpretation: - PmedP_{med} = 0.55: Holding treatment at X=1X = 1, there is a 55% probability that the outcome under the treated mediator level exceeds the outcome under the control mediator level. Since 0.50 represents “no mediation effect”, this indicates a modest positive mediation effect. - Indirect Effect = 0.2: The traditional product-of-coefficients indirect effect (a×ba \times b) quantifies the average change in outcome due to the mediated path.

Workflow Options

probmed offers three workflow approaches to suit your needs:

1. Formula Interface (Recommended for Most Users)

Directly specify your models using R formulas:

result <- pmed(
  Y ~ X + M + C,             # Outcome model
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,     # Mediator model
  data = data,
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap"
)

2. Integration with lavaan (For SEM Users)

Extract from fitted Structural Equation Models with full support for FIML, robust estimators, and standardized estimates:

library(lavaan)

# Define SEM model
model <- '
  M ~ a*X + C
  Y ~ b*M + cp*X + C
'

# Fit with FIML for missing data
fit <- sem(model, data = data, missing = "fiml")

# Extract and compute P_med
extract <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M")
result <- pmed(extract, method = "parametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 5000)
print(result)

3. Integration with mediation Package

Seamlessly work with objects from the mediation package:

library(mediation)

# Fit models
model_m <- lm(M ~ X + C, data = data)
model_y <- lm(Y ~ M + X + C, data = data)

# Run mediate
med_out <- mediate(model_m, model_y, treat = "X", mediator = "M", boot = TRUE)

# Compute P_med from mediate object
result <- pmed(extract_mediation(med_out))
print(result)

Advanced Features

Generalized Linear Models (GLMs)

probmed supports GLMs for non-normal outcomes. For example, with a binary outcome:

# Binary outcome example
data_bin <- data
data_bin$Y_binary <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.4 * data$M + 0.2 * data$X))

result_bin <- pmed(
  Y_binary ~ X + M + C,
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,
  data = data_bin,
  family_y = binomial(),    # Logistic regression for binary outcome
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap",
  n_boot = 1000
)
print(result_bin)

Bootstrap Methods Comparison

When to use each method:

  • Plugin (method = "plugin"): Fast point estimates only, no confidence intervals. Use for quick exploration.
  • Parametric Bootstrap (method = "parametric_bootstrap"): Default choice. Fast and accurate when parameter estimates are approximately normally distributed.
  • Nonparametric Bootstrap (method = "nonparametric_bootstrap"): More robust to distributional assumptions but computationally intensive. Use when parametric assumptions are questionable.
  • MBCO (method = "mbco"): Gaussian models only. Deterministic likelihood-ratio interval; check result@diagnostics for endpoint status.
  • Model-based bootstrap (method = "model_bootstrap", opt-in): simulates complete datasets from the fitted models with the observed treatment and covariates fixed, refits both equations, and reports the percentile interval only when at least 99% of draws are valid. Its coverage has not yet been calibrated.
# Compare methods
result_plugin <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                      treatment = "X", mediator = "M", method = "plugin")

result_param <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                     treatment = "X", mediator = "M",
                     method = "parametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 1000)

result_nonparam <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                        treatment = "X", mediator = "M",
                        method = "nonparametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 1000)
